name: T — retain-all with an investment case, DSCR binds
note:
R13 spec §19. The release's first v10 fixture: a retain-all conversion with a derived investment case (NOI → capitalised value → DSCR/LTV/ICR take-out sizing) rather than the explicit investment_value_pence × ltv_pct pair calc 2.11.0 used. Its LTV-binding twin is u-investment-case-ltv-binds.json — same scheme, same NOI, only the cap yield and the LTV cap change, so the two fixtures prove the binding constraint actually moves rather than being hard-coded.

CASH-FUNDED BY DESIGN (funding_source: 'cash'), not development finance: retain_all plus a levered development facility plus a refinance event is a combination no existing fixture in the corpus exercises, and Task 5b's job is a dependable shared document, not a new facility-interaction proof. A cash deal still exercises the investment case and the refinance event in full — monthly-engine.ts's refinance arm distributes `net_proceeds_pence` whole when `isCash` is true (spec §4.5) — without the extra, untested surface of a facility that may or may not fully redeem against a retained (unsold) scheme. cost_plan is headline mode with no fee lines: this fixture is not about the cost stack, and an empty fee schedule is legal (professional_total/statutory_total both zero) — the same 'an empty schedule is legal' rule §19.7 states for operating_lines.

FIVE RETAINED UNITS, one rent row each, summing to the spec's own worked example: 295,000 pence/month gross potential rent (5 × 59,000). Every unit is retained (route retain_all), satisfying §19.7 rule 2 before that rule exists to enforce it.

FOUR OPERATING LINES spanning both bases: management (10%) and letting_and_re_letting (2%) on pct_of_gross_rent; insurance (25,000) and compliance_and_safety (8,000) on fixed_pence_per_month. NOTE, because it very nearly went unstated: this is NOT the same operating-line set Task 3's cross-engine pinned triple uses (investment-case.test.ts / test_financial_model_investment_case.py's `LINES` constant has only two lines — management 10% and insurance 25,000 fixed — giving NOI 2,758,560). The brief that specified this fixture claimed the fixture and that unit test 'pin the same arithmetic'; they do not, once the fourth line (letting_and_re_letting) and the third (compliance_and_safety) are added on top of Task 3's two. Only the TAKE-OUT parameters below (ltv_cap_pct/dscr_floor/icr_floor/annual_rate_pct/amortisation_years/term_years) are actually identical to Task 3's IO constant; the rent/occupancy/lines chain is this fixture's own, hand-derived below, and does not reproduce Task 3's NOI, value or DSCR-cap figures. Reported as a plan defect rather than silently reconciled.

HAND-DERIVATION (verified against app/financial_model/investment_case.py's already-tested functions, never harvested from run_appraisal — Task 3's engine functions are the unit under test in Task 3, not in this fixture):
  EGR = round(295,000 × 96%) = round(283,200.00) = 283,200 (exact — 295,000 × 96 = 28,320,000, ÷100 exact)
  opex = round(283,200 × 10%) + round(283,200 × 2%) + 25,000 + 8,000
       = 28,320 + 5,664 + 25,000 + 8,000 = 66,984
  stabilised monthly NOI = 283,200 − 66,984 = 216,216
  stabilised annual NOI = 12 × 216,216 = 2,594,592 pence
  investment value = round(2,594,592 × 100 / 5.5 / 1.0675)
                    = round(259,459,200 / 5.5 / 1.0675) = round(47,174,400 / 1.0675)
                    = round(44,191,475.41) = 44,191,475 pence
  a (annual debt service factor, 25y amortising @ 6%) = 12 × i/(1−(1+i)^−300), i = 0.005
                    = 0.0773161681... (closed form; independent of NOI/value)
  r = 0.06
  LTV cap  = floor(44,191,475 × 65 / 100) = floor(28,724,458.75)  = 28,724,458
  DSCR cap = floor(2,594,592 / (1.3 × 0.0773161682)) = floor(2,594,592 / 0.10051102) = 25,814,005
  ICR cap  = floor(2,594,592 / (1.3 × 0.06))          = floor(2,594,592 / 0.078)     = 33,264,000 (exact: 0.078 × 33,264,000 = 2,594,592.0)
  min(28,724,458 ; 25,814,005 ; 33,264,000) = 25,814,005 = DSCR cap → BINDING CONSTRAINT = 'dscr'.

PROGRAMME: a straight-line, twelve-phase precedence network (no float, no anchor tricks — that is anchoredSlippedDoc()'s job, not this fixture's), acquisition(1mo)→planning(2)→conditions(1)→design(2)→procurement(1)→strip_out(1)→construction(6)→building_control(1)→practical_completion(0, milestone)→unit_completions(2)→sales(3)→maturity_tail(0). Forward pass: starts 0,1,3,4,6,7,8,14,15,15,17,20; practical_completion starts month 15. Stabilisation is anchored to practical_completion + 1 = month 16, ramp_months 3 (occupancy ramps months 16-18, stabilised from month 18). facility term_months 24 gives comfortable headroom against both the overrun rule (programme finish 21 ≤ 24) and the sale-tail rule (practical_completion start 15 ≤ term−2 = 22; building_control finish 15 ≤ term−1 = 23). The refinance event sits at month 20, two months after the ramp completes.

COST STACK, chosen (not derived from any existing pin) for a clean implied rate: 5 units × 70 sqm = 350 sqm; construction_cost_per_sqm_pence 100,000 → base_build 35,000,000; general contingency 10% → 3,500,000; construction_total 38,500,000; empty fee schedule → professional/statutory 0; conversion_total 38,500,000. lender_eligible_base_pence is 0 in headline mode by construction (computeCostPlan sums `packages[].amount_pence` for lender-eligible packages, and headline mode carries no packages — this is not a claim about lender eligibility, only about the mode). implied_rate = round(35,000,000 / 350) = 100,000 pence/sqm.

WHAT THIS FIXTURE DOES NOT COVER: the investment_case RESULT block (Schedule.investment_case, AppraisalResultV2.investment_case) does not exist until Tasks 8/11 land, so expected_metrics below pins only what run_appraisal can produce TODAY — gdv_pence and the cost_plan headline figures. The investment-case pins (annual_noi_pence, investment_value_pence, binding_constraint) are the fixture's whole reason to exist and are deferred to Task 8 or 11, which add the result block this note's hand-derivation above already anticipates.
